name: Mindat
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Jordan, M. 1969. Chin dictionary and grammar (Mindat Cho); also Mang Kee Shein 2006, Payap Univ.

sources.note: Used only to identify the report as JLSR 2021-049 (hhtype wordlist;socling).

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Julius Dabet, Adedamola Aregbesola, Thelma Araokanmi & Danielle Gootjes. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Duhwa [kbz], Mindat [mmf], and Sya [scw] Languages of Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-049. Dallas: SIL International. 59 pp.
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 8.2 (pp. 17-18) gives only consonant and Mindat vowel phone charts, vowel length, prenasalisation/labialisation/palatalisation; App. E p. 32: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Tone diacritics on the 348-item Mindat wordlist; zero hits for stress/accent/prosody/syllable. Sec. 3: 'It does not appear that anyone has done further significant linguistic research on these Ron languages.'

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019 [file 2020]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 328 Mundat (PDF p. 100).
sources.note: Entry gives only location (Plateau State, Mangu LGA) and classification (Chadic: West A: Ron group); no Source(s) or Ref(s) lines at all, i.e. Blench lists no linguistic literature for Mundat. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. n.d. [file dated 2009]. Ron comparative wordlist (Daffo-Butura, Bokkos, Monguna, Sha, Mundat, Karfa, Mangar, Richa, Fyer, Tambas, *proto-Ron). Unpublished ms., 37 pp.
sources.note: Bare tone-marked wordlist with a Mundat column; no prose on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2003. Why reconstructing comparative Ron is so problematic. In H. Ekkehard Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics: Papers from the 1st Biennial International Colloquium on the Chadic Languages, Leipzig 2001, 21-42. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.note: Mundat is one of ten Ron lects compared (Western Ron with Sha and Karfa; Table 10 Mundat-Karfa innovations). Sec. 3.3 Tones p. 28: 'All attested Ron languages have three level tones as well as combination tones and this can therefore be posited in Proto-Ron.' No mention of stress/accent.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. Unpublished Ron field data (Mundat, Sha, Karfa wordlists and notes, 1998-2001) referred to in Blench 2003 ('much data available... most of it unpublished') and used by Decker et al. 2021.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only first-hand linguistic data on Mundat beyond the SIL 348-item list; if any phonology notes exist for Mundat they are in Blench's files (Kay Williamson Educational Foundation), not published.

sources.citation: Seibert, Uwe. 1998. Das Ron von Daffo (Jos-Plateau, Zentralnigeria). Europäische Hochschulschriften XXI/66 [XXVII/66]. Frankfurt am Main: Peter Lang. XIV+166 pp. (Kap. I Das Lautsystem, pp. 8-18)

sources.note: Modern description of a sister Ron lect (Daffo) with a Lautsystem chapter (Ton, Silbe); would show whether Ron specialists treat the group as purely tonal with no word stress, and its bibliography lists all Ron work incl. any unpublished Mundat/Sha notes by Seibert.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 1970. Die Ron-Sprachen: tschadohamitische Studien in Nordnigerien. Afrikanistische Forschungen 3. Glückstadt: J.J. Augustin. xviii+429 pp. (esp. Abschnitt 4 'Zur Sprache der Scha (SYA)', pp. 231-294, and the general introduction)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only book-length description of the Ron group; Mundat has no chapter of its own but is named in it (per Decker et al. 2021) and its closest described relative Sha/Sya has a 60-page section. Any incidental Ton/Akzent remark applying to Western Ron would be here; the Fyer chapter is the only one with explicit 'Zur Phonologie'/'Zur Tonologie' headings.
